parts.title: Millions of Living Things. Only 4 Groups? (Part 1) | Classifying Living Things
parts.description:
There are millions of kinds of living things, but scientists sort them into only four main groups. Can you name all four? Open the four crates with Pip, Basil and Momo. Part 1 of Primary 3 Science, Diversity: classification of living things.

In this part:
• Why scientists classify living things
• The four main groups: plants, animals, fungi and bacteria
• Shrink down until you are as tiny as bacteria
• What makes a plant a plant

Key words: classification, fungi, bacteria.
Watch Part 2 to find out if a plant with no flowers today can be a flowering plant!

TheOneApp, Explained: Singapore primary science, made fun. Play along with Pip, Basil and Momo: point to lock in, keep score on your hand, beat the Buddies! Practise this topic in TheOneApp.

Singapore Primary 3 Science (2023 syllabus): Diversity, classification of living things (Chapter 2, pp. 19–22). Also fits US NGSS 4-LS1-1.
Try it for real: find one flowering plant and one non-flowering plant near your home. Look, do not pick. Sort plants yourself in TheOneApp: School Lab 2.1A, Bloom or not.
For the curious: a scientist called Linnaeus gave every living thing a two-part name. Humans are Homo sapiens.

parts.title: No Flowers Today. Is It a FLOWERING Plant? (Part 2) | Flowering and Non-Flowering Plants
parts.description:
This chilli plant has no flowers today. So is it a flowering plant or a non-flowering plant? Part 2 of Primary 3 Science, Diversity: classification of living things.

In this part:
• Flowering plants: flowers, fruits and seeds
• Non-flowering plants: spores in spore bags
• Be a fern spore: ride the wind and land on damp soil
• Is grass a flowering plant?

Key words: flowering plants, non-flowering plants, spore bags.
Watch Part 1 first!
